title: Quarter Cascade and Town Sprint Brief (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight operational brief to: 1) propose a repeatable quarterly cascade format that ties executive priorities to team-level commitments (OKRs), 2) outline the cadence and content for the company town sprint (a focused all-hands + follow-up week), and 3) list concrete deliverables, comms, and owners for the next quarter kickoff.

Context / Why this format:
- We have varied approaches to cascade across departments; this is an experiment to standardize one 2-week sprint around the all-hands that produces: an executive update, aligned OKR drafts for each org, a short roadmap highlight, and a set of cross-team dependency tickets.
- Emphasis: speed of alignment over polished artifacts. The goal is actionable commitments and a prioritized risk register.

High-level timeline (proposed):
- Week -2 (Pre-sprint): Execs prepare 2-slide priority brief + 3 signal metrics. Team leads draft OKRs in the shared template.
- Week -1 (Sync week): Leadership review sessions (30–45m) with each org. Consolidate cross-team dependencies. Finalize town agenda.
- Town Sprint Week (Day 0 = All-Hands):
  - 09:00: Opening (CEO) — lens on business thesis and top-3 company priorities for the quarter (10m)
  - 09:15: Executive 2-slide rapid updates (CTO, Head of Product, Head of Sales + 5m each)
  - 10:00: Breakouts by org (30m) — teams present their top OKR drafts and blockers
  - 10:40: Live Q&A and commitment capture (20m)
  - 11:10: Customer highlight + ops update (20m)
  - Afternoon: Team kickoff sessions (facilitated) to turn town input into concrete tickets and owners.
- Week +1: Follow-up week — teams convert commitments into tracked OKRs (in the template) and file cross-team tickets. Execs review and mark any unresolved dependencies.

Draft Company-level OKRs (starter, for discussion):
- Objective A: Make inference predictable and cost-efficient for growing PLG customers.
  - KR1: Reduce 95th percentile API latency for small requests by 18%.
  - KR2: Lower per-1M-token hosted cost by 12% via batching + cache improvements.
  - KR3: Ship 2 new model-variants in catalog with verified perf profiles.

- Objective B: Expand private deployment readiness and enterprise GTM motion.
  - KR1: Complete Private VPC onboarding flow for 3 pilot customers (including KMS).
  - KR2: Publish compliance package (SOC/ISO checklist) + one-page sales playbook.
  - KR3: Close first Dedicated reserved contract > $XXk ARR.

Notes on OKR drafting guidance to teams:
- Keep each org to 3 objectives max. Each KR should be measurable and have a named owner.
- Mix output KRs (deliverables) and outcome KRs (metric change). Avoid more than 5 KRs per objective.
- Highlight cross-team dependencies with an explicit impact statement.

Deliverables (owner + due):
- Executive 2-slide briefs (Lena Ortiz) — due Week -2 (2025-11-17).
- Team OKR drafts (team leads) — due Week -2 (add to shared sheet).
- Town agenda + facilitator pack (Marcus Rey) — due Week -1 (2025-11-24).
- Dependency register (sheet) and ticket seeds (product + infra leads) — due Town+3 days (2025-12-02).
- Communications bundle (email + intranet post + slide deck) (Priya Kapoor) — ready Day 0 morning.

Pre-reads and templates:
- Use the shared OKR template: (link in linked_artifacts).
- Pre-read expectations: 1 page: top-3 risks, 2 signal metrics, 3 proposed OKRs. Keep it short.

Town Sprint facilitation notes (working cues):
- Encourage teams to state the single biggest ask they need from another org. Capture that verbatim into the dependency register.
- Timebox presentations strictly. We prefer more small breakout conversations over long single-speaker sessions.
- Rotate facilitators from non-executive staff to build cadence and speed.

Comms plan (internal):
- Announcement email from CEO 1-week before town with high-level goals.
- Day-of short digest sent at 16:00 with commitments captured and next steps.
- Run a 10-minute onboarding for new hires on Day +1 about how we run quarterly cadence and where to find OKR artifacts.

Metrics to monitor during the sprint:
- Participation: % of teams that submitted OKR draft by Week -2. Target > 90%.
- Resolution: % of cross-team dependencies with owners assigned by Week +1. Target > 85%.
- Quality: Exec satisfaction (quick 5-question pulse) at end of Day 0. Target score >= 4/5.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Teams treat OKR draft as optional -> low participation. Mitigation: Execs to call out missing drafts in reviews and escalate to managers.
- Risk: Over-engineered pre-reads slow teams down. Mitigation: Strict 1-page pre-read rule and a template enforced by company-ops.
- Risk: Town becomes presentation-heavy and lacks action. Mitigation: enforce breakout structure and commit to follow-up ticketing before end of Day+1.

Post-sprint governance:
- Company-ops maintains dependency register and runs weekly unblock meetings for the first 6 weeks of the quarter.
- Quarterly review: execs provide a short 2-slide retrospective on what worked / didn't at the next town.

Open questions for review (please comment):
1) Should the town sprint be 1 full day or 2 half-days to accommodate APAC? Pros/cons?
2) Do we want product-hosted-api to publish an SLO ladder for public benchmarking at town?
3) Are there legal/compliance pre-reads that must be mandatory for Private deals before the sprint?

Next steps (owners):
- Approve cadence and publish this brief (Lena) — by 2025-11-19.
- Circulate executive 2-slide template and examples (Marcus) — by 2025-11-17.
- All team leads to confirm OKR lead and submit draft (team leads) — by 2025-11-17.

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Could introduce a short ‘green/yellow/red’ status flag for each KR to simplify weekly tracking.
- Consider a one-page public-facing summary to use in partner briefings (smaller subset of company priorities).
- Try rotating the town time next quarter to include a late afternoon APAC-friendly session.

This draft seeks feedback from execs and team leads. Please add comments inline or ping me directly in Slack.
